title: Keysight Unites RF and Photonic Design for Tower Semiconductor
gist: Keysight certified its ADS Photonic Designer for Tower Semiconductor's PH18 silicon photonics PDK (announced November 9), letting RF/high-speed designers co-simulate electronics and photonics in one electrical-optical-electrical flow — relevant as data center links push to 1.6 Tb/s and co-packaged optics — though the article stresses there are no quantified customer results yet.

insights.claim: Keysight certified its Advanced Design System (ADS) Photonic Designer for Tower Semiconductor's PH18 silicon photonics PDK, announced November 9, enabling schematic-to-simulation-to-layout flows covering both electronic and photonic circuits; the PH18 kit is available now.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Incremental ecosystem win for Tower's silicon photonics platform and Keysight EDA.
insights.locator: Keysight Technologies has certified its Advanced Design System

insights.claim: Tower's RF technologies have been supported in ADS for more than a decade, so the photonics extension lets existing ADS users add Tower photonics to an established workflow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Lowers adoption friction for Tower photonics among RF designers already on ADS.

insights.claim: Final foundry verification and tapeout for PH18 designs remain in Tower's tools, with ADS handling system simulation, design-rule-compliant photonic layout elements and layout-versus-schematic comparisons.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Keysight complements rather than displaces foundry signoff flows.
insights.locator: The PH18 integration connects those investigations

insights.claim: Because drivers, modulators, optical channels, detectors and amplifiers all shape the final optical-link signal, evaluating components separately can hide interactions; Keysight's electrical-optical-electrical simulation models the full signal chain in ADS.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: System-level co-simulation becomes a differentiator in optical interconnect design tools.
insights.quote: Evaluating individual components separately can obscure interactions that determine whether the complete connection meets its performance target.
insights.locator: Optical communications still depend on electronics

insights.claim: As data center interconnects move toward 1.6 terabits per second and beyond, faster links leave less margin for signal degradation and AI infrastructure raises pressure to deliver bandwidth efficiently, increasing the value of joint electronic-photonic analysis.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: 1.6T optics transition is a demand driver for photonic EDA and silicon photonics foundries.

insights.claim: Keysight's Photonic Designer materials cite co-packaged optics and near-package optics as target applications for the integrated workflow.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Ties the tooling to the CPO build-out theme.
insights.locator: The announcement also supports the industry’s interest

insights.claim: The main potential benefit is catching interface or performance bottlenecks in simulation before fabrication, reducing respins, but the announcement provides no quantified customer results or independent benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Treat claimed time and cost savings as unverified until customer data appears.
insights.quote: the announcement provides no quantified customer results or independent benchmarks establishing those savings

insights.claim: The author says the strategic implications — easier Tower photonics adoption for ADS users, stronger Keysight foundry ties — are reasonable inferences, not evidence of new customers or revenue for either company.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: No near-term revenue read-through; watch for named design wins.
insights.quote: These are reasonable implications of the integration, rather than evidence that either company has already secured additional customers or revenue.

insights.claim: Success of the integration will depend on model accuracy, usable workflows and agreement between simulated behavior and fabricated hardware.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Model-to-silicon correlation is the metric to track.
